#/head: the residency CREATE: a bag takes a fresh coordinate, empty

`CREATE` mints a new bag at a fresh coordinate, empty, with its identity a fresh document URL; registration lands as a `holdings` accession in the union catalog. `--plane` picks the bag's plane, `catalog` or `oracle`; any other word refuses. A caller inside the CLI that read the bag off the canon source as house canon (the seed) carries that claim on the verb, and an island that never seated the bag refuses `house-canon-unseated` and mints no catalog row. CREATE carries no content to tell one change from the next, so `--change-id` folds into the effect key's nonce.

`declare <bag>` writes (or amends) the bag's own declaration: `--tier` (its cap-tier), `--home` (one of the homes a bag may name), `--repo` (a REGISTERED repo id, never a directory; an unregistered id refuses), `--role` (one line). It wants at least one of the four. Declaring moves NO bytes: relocation takes `lares bag home`, and a declaration that now disagrees with where the bytes sit marks the bag ADRIFT. A standing daemon re-stamps the catalog row at once (`restamp-bag-tier`), so a tier change takes the row's stamp; with no daemon the next boot stamps it.
The reserved TW5 docs name refuses (`bag declare`).

cure: lares bag declare <bag> --tier private
home-unknown  --home expects one of the homes a bag may name
repo-unregistered  the repo id stands registered on no vessel here; register it first
cure: carriage.bag.registers

`declare <bag>` writes (or amends) the bag's own declaration: `--tier` (its cap-tier), `--home` (one of the homes a bag may name), `--repo` (a REGISTERED repo id, never a directory; an unregistered id refuses), `--role` (one line). It wants at least one of the four. Declaring moves NO bytes: relocation takes `lares bag home`, and a declaration that now disagrees with where the bytes sit marks the bag ADRIFT. A standing daemon re-stamps the catalog row at once (`restamp-bag-tier`), so a tier change takes the row's stamp; with no daemon the next boot stamps it.
The reserved TW5 docs name refuses (`bag declare`).
Examples:
<$ bag="lares" tier="private"/>    # declare the bag's cap-tier
<$ bag="lares" home="repository" repo="lares-repo"/>    # declare the bag's home as a registered repo
Arguments:
bag <slug>  the bag to declare
tier <cap-tier>  the bag's cap-tier; it only ever tightens against the structural floor
home <home>  where the bag belongs
repo <repo-id>  a registered repo's id; the declaration carries the id and never a path
role <words>  one line naming what the bag holds
Gate (the carrier's testimony; the door checks):
write: a local write of the bag's own declaration beside its bytes; moves nothing

declare-nothing  declare wants something to declare: --tier, --home, --repo or --role

repo-unregistered  the repo id stands registered on no vessel here; register it first
cure: <$carriage.bag.registers/>

declared (exit 0)  the declaration written; adrift names a mismatch with the bytes, restamp what the catalog row took

#/head: the move that relocates bytes and re-anchors the declaration together

`home <bag> --to <home>` MOVES the bytes to a declared home and re-anchors the declaration together. It plans before it touches anything (the DRY-RUN default prints the plan and the command that performs it) and refuses an occupied destination rather than merging. `--approve` performs the move, and no source-control verb ever runs: the bytes land in a working tree, and what enters a history stays the hand's own act. `--repo` names the registered repo id where the home reads repository.
The move relocates an operator's bytes across a boundary that matters (into a tracked history, or out of one), so it earns the explicit approval.

#/head: the residency MOVE: an atomic ADD to the destination and a CLEAR from the source

`MOVE` pairs an ADD to the destination with a CLEAR of the title from the source, as one transfer: a live source lands its whole family in the destination (the root and its component slots) and retracts the family to absent in the source; the change-id travels, and one transfer-id ties the accession to the deaccession. A MOVE that names `--from` and `--to` and no `--title` promotes the WHOLE source layer, every live title it holds, in one act.

A MOVE of a tombstone carries a delete down: `--title` and `--from` with `--to` name the bag where the delete takes place; with no `--to` the bags holding the title print as candidates (and the line asks for --to). `--shadow` hides a title from a bag that holds none, a delete that shadows the lower layers, and rides a title-grain MOVE alone: a layer move, or any other verb, refuses it.
A terminal asks `Proceed? [y/N]` before it submits; `--yes` names the intent off a terminal, `--dry-run` previews and commits nothing, `--in-wiki` runs the act in the active wiki's island.

lares act MOVE — move a tiddler, or a whole layer, to another bag; promotion rides here
the residency MOVE: an atomic ADD to the destination and a CLEAR from the source

`MOVE` pairs an ADD to the destination with a CLEAR of the title from the source, as one transfer: a live source lands its whole family in the destination (the root and its component slots) and retracts the family to absent in the source; the change-id travels, and one transfer-id ties the accession to the deaccession. A MOVE that names `--from` and `--to` and no `--title` promotes the WHOLE source layer, every live title it holds, in one act.

A MOVE of a tombstone carries a delete down: `--title` and `--from` with `--to` name the bag where the delete takes place; with no `--to` the bags holding the title print as candidates (and the line asks for --to). `--shadow` hides a title from a bag that holds none, a delete that shadows the lower layers, and rides a title-grain MOVE alone: a layer move, or any other verb, refuses it.
A terminal asks `Proceed? [y/N]` before it submits; `--yes` names the intent off a terminal, `--dry-run` previews and commits nothing, `--in-wiki` runs the act in the active wiki's island.
Examples:

lares act MOVE --title lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/docs/pono/example --from lar:///ha.ka.ba/wikis/lares/working --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares    # land the title in the destination and retract it from the source
lares act MOVE --from lar:///ha.ka.ba/wikis/lares/working --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares    # move every live title the source layer holds, as a promotion
lares act MOVE --title lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/docs/pono/example --from lar:///ha.ka.ba/wikis/lares/working    # with no destination, print the bags holding the title as candidates for the delete
lares act MOVE --title lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/docs/pono/example --from lar:///ha.ka.ba/wikis/lares/working --shadow    # hide the title from a bag that holds none

`cas` is a local read over the cleartext `cid/` CAS tier, with no daemon boot: it lists the blobs the CAS dir holds and DERIVES which the disk projection references (a `.tid` or `.meta` under `bags/` or `wikis/` carrying `textCid`, or a `lar:///…/cid/<hash>` `_canonical_uri`), then reports blobs · referenced · unreferenced · pending · bytes, and names the genesis-manifest blobs as protected (the engine and plugins never sweep). `export <dest>` carries the operator's AUTHORED memory out before a re-founding. It writes a bundle outside the house root and the workspace: the daemon mount's wiki working carriers, the kāpae shadows and canon carriers, its kahua stage heads, draft recovery files, consented temp carriers, and house-minted bags, with a roster (the re-declare list of pet-names, Handles and chair labels, plus the share rows) sealed under the house's keep key (`<config>/keep-key`). Faces ride by path key, never by a key or a face relation, and the verb reads every byte back against its manifest before it answers.

It waits for a settled projection: an unsettled carrier or a held save refuses by name unless `--accept-omissions` names the bundle partial, and the manifest records each omission. A face whose live stage will not read cuts with no flag: its files travel, its standing heads stay behind as a counted `face-unread` omission, and this terminal alone names the face. Sensoriums never travel (they survive where they stand), and neither does the daemon document or the control document. The bundle rests UNENCRYPTED, private memory as plain files: keep it on a disk only you hold, and remove it once imported.

#/head: the pack's collect-the-residency export: a foreign bundle takes the round trip

A multi-tiddler bundle (a `.json` array of tiddlers, or a `.multids`) rides as a PACK: one file, many tiddlers, whose membership rests ASIDE in the bag's `$:/config/OriginalTiddlerPaths`, never on the tiddlers. `REPACK` asks the island to collect the pack's members from that aside map and re-render the bundle through TW5's own serializer, then writes the bytes to disk: the deliberate round trip a foreign bundle takes before an upstream TW5 PR (a `.mem` path recomposes by itself; a foreign pack re-renders on this verb alone).

The pack path derives from the file's mirror-relative address plus its extension, so the source sits under `bags/` or `wikis/`; `--out` names where the bytes land and defaults to the source. REPACK registers as a QUERY verb (read cap, no residency mutation, no effect record), so it asks no `Proceed?` and carries no effect key; only a fresh request id rides each attempt, and a repeat stays safe. Members the bag tombstoned print as missing.

#/head: the disk-to-records gesture: scan, diff, preview, then apply through the gate

The gesture holds the disk grant and the Synced tree (the island holds neither; readiness reads local on both sides of the shore). It scans the source for `.mem` carriers, derives each address by the address-siting rule, and diffs the disk hash against the synced hash per carrier. The default posture PREVIEWS: it prints NEW, UNCHANGED and CHANGED rows and submits nothing. `--apply` sends the NEW and CHANGED carriers, their hashes riding an INGEST verb, and the island runs the full Confluence gate (its currentRenderHash stands as the third leg) and answers per carrier.

`--tag-blobs` stamps the CAS opt-in flag (a `.meta` sidecar, or a meme's ahu meta) on the large un-flagged carriers that would fault during LOAD or INGEST; it writes no records, and the preview names the count. `--watch` fires the same gesture per settled wave instead of once: one wave per quiet window (`--debounce` ms), preview by default, `--apply` submits. A file that vanished tombstones nothing: the watcher hands it to the vessel's shore, where it stands pending until a person answers with `lares shore remove` or `lares shore restore`. A file that holds no base never lands over records that say something else, and a file that moved while the records moved never lands: each stands off at the vessel's shore (`lares shore`), and every wave says no person stands behind it (`unattended`). `--in-wiki` runs the INGEST in the active wiki's island, the path for the working write-layer ingest-back (a `wikis/` source derives its URIs off that layer).

The one-shot flags (`--yes`, `--tag-blobs`, `--in-wiki`, `--change-id`) ride the one-shot ingest and refuse beside `--watch`; `--debounce` rides `--watch` alone. A scan that skipped every carrier answers usage and names the mirror directories it derived against, since the source must sit under the bags dir (LAR_BAGS) or wikis dir (LAR_WIKIS) as `<holding>/<w.w.w>/…/<name>.<ext>`.

whole: Scan disk into records through the Confluence gate

The gesture holds the disk grant and the Synced tree (the island holds neither; readiness reads local on both sides of the shore). It scans the source for `.mem` carriers, derives each address by the address-siting rule, and diffs the disk hash against the synced hash per carrier. The default posture PREVIEWS: it prints NEW, UNCHANGED and CHANGED rows and submits nothing. `--apply` sends the NEW and CHANGED carriers, their hashes riding an INGEST verb, and the island runs the full Confluence gate (its currentRenderHash stands as the third leg) and answers per carrier.

`--tag-blobs` stamps the CAS opt-in flag (a `.meta` sidecar, or a meme's ahu meta) on the large un-flagged carriers that would fault during LOAD or INGEST; it writes no records, and the preview names the count. `--watch` fires the same gesture per settled wave instead of once: one wave per quiet window (`--debounce` ms), preview by default, `--apply` submits. A file that vanished tombstones nothing: the watcher hands it to the vessel's shore, where it stands pending until a person answers with `lares shore remove` or `lares shore restore`. A file that holds no base never lands over records that say something else, and a file that moved while the records moved never lands: each stands off at the vessel's shore (`lares shore`), and every wave says no person stands behind it (`unattended`). `--in-wiki` runs the INGEST in the active wiki's island, the path for the working write-layer ingest-back (a `wikis/` source derives its URIs off that layer).

The one-shot flags (`--yes`, `--tag-blobs`, `--in-wiki`, `--change-id`) ride the one-shot ingest and refuse beside `--watch`; `--debounce` rides `--watch` alone. A scan that skipped every carrier answers usage and names the mirror directories it derived against, since the source must sit under the bags dir (LAR_BAGS) or wikis dir (LAR_WIKIS) as `<holding>/<w.w.w>/…/<name>.<ext>`.

Gate (the carrier's testimony; the door checks): write: --apply writes records through the island's gate, which checks the cap on the destination bag; a preview, --tag-blobs aside, writes none. disk: the command holds the disk grant: it reads the source tree on the host, the island reads none.
Refuses: usage · watch-one-shot · debounce-alone.
Answers band: previewed · applied · standoff.

#/answers: listed (exit 0)  every row, each naming its island; a standoff names its key and a pending removal the commit that took its file, where one did
#/gate: read: a read: the vessel looks at the disk and names what stands; it writes nothing
#/head: what stands for a hand at the disk shore

The vessel looks at the disk first, so the list stands true to the bytes at that instant, then names every row the shore holds: each STANDOFF (the disk and the records say different things and nothing writes) with its key, and each PENDING REMOVAL (a file vanished where a base stands; nothing writes back and nothing tombstones). Both islands read as one shore, every page of each, each row naming its island (`wiki`, the active wiki's mirrors; `daemon`, the daemon wiki's and the crossroads). A bare `lares shore` lists.

`--face N` names a LIT SIBLING's shore by handle index: its own projector answers in the daemon island with no wear, and a face that stands no projection refuses `face-unprojected`. `--bag` narrows to one bag. The list refuses to state a shore nobody measured: rows with no count, a page with no mark, a cursor that stands still, or rows short of the counts refuse `shore-list-unpaged`, and a mark that moves mid-read refuses `shore-list-moved`. Where a commit took a pending removal's file from its checkout, the row names that commit beside it (short sha, subject, PR, and the ashes git keeps) as `retiredBy`.
A seat reads the shore through `shore`; the answers that settle a row stay a person's hand at a terminal, so a seat names the command for the operator.

The vessel looks at the disk first, so the list stands true to the bytes at that instant, then names every row the shore holds: each STANDOFF (the disk and the records say different things and nothing writes) with its key, and each PENDING REMOVAL (a file vanished where a base stands; nothing writes back and nothing tombstones). Both islands read as one shore, every page of each, each row naming its island (`wiki`, the active wiki's mirrors; `daemon`, the daemon wiki's and the crossroads). A bare `lares shore` lists.

`--face N` names a LIT SIBLING's shore by handle index: its own projector answers in the daemon island with no wear, and a face that stands no projection refuses `face-unprojected`. `--bag` narrows to one bag. The list refuses to state a shore nobody measured: rows with no count, a page with no mark, a cursor that stands still, or rows short of the counts refuse `shore-list-unpaged`, and a mark that moves mid-read refuses `shore-list-moved`. Where a commit took a pending removal's file from its checkout, the row names that commit beside it (short sha, subject, PR, and the ashes git keeps) as `retiredBy`.
A seat reads the shore through `shore`; the answers that settle a row stay a person's hand at a terminal, so a seat names the command for the operator.

$tw.lares.call("carriage.disk.reads", {"bag": "lares"})    # narrow the list to one bag

#/answers: took (exit 0)  the file's side won; the line names the carrier and its bag
aborted (exit 1)  the person answered no at the prompt
#/gate: hand-act: a settling act reads the hand behind this command before anything else; an AI harness on its branch refuses hand-act-only, an unreadable branch hand-unattested, each naming the command the operator runs, and --yes approves nothing by itself
#/head: a person settles one standoff toward the disk

`take-disk <uri> --key <key>` lands the file's words in the records for one standoff, riding the worn face's ingest leg. `keep-disk` lands the file's words WHOLE, with no merge, and lets the standoff's drafts go. A standoff first loads the file's side as drafts in the worn face's draft layer, and the collapse rules the person set in their daemon face (`$:/config/lares/shore/collapse/<rule>`) settle what they can; what stays raises one alert naming `keep-disk`, `keep-records`, and where drafts stand `keep-both` and `drafts`.

Where no base stands, `lares ingest` of the file names the same adoption. SETTLING STAYS A HAND ACT: the verb reads the hand behind this command first; an AI harness on its branch refuses `hand-act-only`, an unreadable branch `hand-unattested`, and `--yes` approves nothing by itself. A terminal asks `Proceed? [y/N]` (the records give way to the file's present words); a JSON call off a terminal needs `--yes`. The key comes from the alert; an answer that names a state that moved takes nothing.
#/refuses: hand-act-only  an AI harness settles nothing; the line names the command the operator runs
cure: carriage.disk.reads
hand-unattested  the branch behind this command stays unreadable; read the shore, then run the act on your own terminal
cure: carriage.disk.reads
usage  a carrier and the standoff's key both stand required
cure: lares shore take-disk <uri> --key <key>
a-state-that-moved  an answer names the state its giver read (a standoff's key, or the count that stands pending); where that state moved, the island refuses by name and nothing changes

A standoff first loads the file's side as drafts in the worn face's draft layer, and the collapse rules the person set in their daemon face (`$:/config/lares/shore/collapse/<rule>`) settle what they can; what stays raises one alert naming `keep-disk`, `keep-records`, and where drafts stand `keep-both` and `drafts`.

Where no base stands, `lares ingest` of the file names the same adoption. SETTLING STAYS A HAND ACT: the verb reads the hand behind this command first; an AI harness on its branch refuses `hand-act-only`, an unreadable branch `hand-unattested`, and `--yes` approves nothing by itself. A terminal asks `Proceed? [y/N]` (the records give way to the file's present words); a JSON call off a terminal needs `--yes`. The key comes from the alert; an answer that names a state that moved takes nothing.

lares shore take-disk lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/docs/pono/example --key <key>    # the file's words land in the records

The residency model derives its verbs from SPARQL Update over (title × bag). `ADD` grants one tiddler residency in the destination bag while the source bag retains its copy: the tiddler's Work-level identity travels, so downstream tooling reads the landing as the same change in a second bag, never a new record. The verb takes the title, the source bag, the destination bag and a change-id (named, or minted when absent), submits one verb-tiddler to the vessel, and the wiki island's action-handler family runs it wrapped in an effect record that writes the archival audit tiddlers (an `accession` row on the destination).

A terminal asks `Proceed? [y/N]` before it submits; `--yes` names the intent for a call off a terminal, `--dry-run` previews the effect and commits nothing, and `--in-wiki` runs the act in the active wiki's island. Run `lares act` for the door's index of every residency action.

#/answers: put (exit 0)  the record landed; decision reads put
noop (exit 0)  the record already says it; nothing moved
family (exit 0)  a family text landed through the Confluence gate and resealed
conflict (exit 4)  the base read stale; the live hash rides the answer and nothing landed
dry (exit 0)  a dry put: the answer the real put would give, the base it needs and the carrier's seat hints; nothing landed
exists (exit 4)  create met a standing record; nothing landed
#/gate: write: the Kahu predicate, then the face's write cap on the bag the cascade lands in, wikis first: the working layer
#/head: the one write path: text, a span, an append, fields and tags, under a base

A put patches one record: it sets and unsets fields, adds and removes tags, and moves the text only where `text`, `file`, `append` or `replace` names it. Every field the patch leaves unnamed stays as it stood, so a field or tag patch never touches the text and a text put keeps the fields. The write lands in the wiki's working layer (`wiki status` names it), or this face's personal layer of a wiki where it holds no writer's seat, and the receipt's `layer` names that placement; `bag` lands in that one bag through its store, under the gates its own writes keep. A seat's write aimed at a house canon bag refuses `seat-canon-reach`: a seat reaches canon through a recipe's copy-up and `meme_offer`. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

`base` carries the hash last read (a record's `hash`, a root's carrier `canonicalHash`; a slot read's partial base `partial:#/x:…` patches within its span and refuses `base-outside-span` beyond it): a record that moved past it answers `conflict`, naming the live hash, and nothing lands. A base guards honest reuse, never a lock. `create` lands only where no record stands, a family's root included; one standing answers `exists`.

`append` lands words at the end of the standing text with no base, read and written in one step on the live wiki, so two appends at once both land, in the order the record took them; a text that does not end on a newline takes one before the words. A terminal reads the words from a host path, or `-` for stdin; a seat names them. It names its words alone (`text`, `file`, `base`, `fields`, `unset` beside it refuse); `tag-add`, `tag-remove` and `create` ride beside it, and a missing title refuses unless `create` names it. Each call appends again.

`replace` names one exact span of the standing text and `with` the words it turns into (an empty `with` removes the span); the rest of the text never crosses the wire. The span counts as written, never trimmed, overlaps counted: zero refuses `replace-absent`, more than one `replace-ambiguous`, each naming the count and the read that cures it, and nothing moves. The result lands as a text put does, under the same base, and the receipt names `replaced`.

A meme family moves by the same put. A whole carrier as a root's text lands the family through the Confluence gate (the family re-splits and reseals; the answer adds `canonicalHash`, `landed`, `kept`, `tombstoned`); `slot` folds into the title (`<root>#/x`), so a slot's text lands with no base and an append honours the slot's standing postamble. Absence never deletes: a slot the new text omits stays standing by reference, named under `kept`, and `cut-slot` names each slot that leaves (a cut naming no standing omitted slot refuses `cut-not-omitted`). A family under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/<class>/<slug>` follows `stage-path-shape`.

The fences refuse by name: a family's `type` and carriage fields derive from its text (`family-carriage-derives`); a new slot joins through its parent's text (`family-joins-by-text`); a text the gate cannot read as one carrier refuses `family-gate-refused`; a title that stays home refuses `tiddler-withheld`; a put over a rendered tiddler, or one carrying `rendered-from`, refuses `rendered-derives`, since only the renderer writes it: edit the source records. Every other shape lands natively, a `$:/` title or tag, a module or plugin field and a script type alike. A put writes the face it wears and never another (`cross-face-write-refused`).

A put patches one record: it sets and unsets fields, adds and removes tags, and moves the text only where `text`, `file`, `append` or `replace` names it. Every field the patch leaves unnamed stays as it stood, so a field or tag patch never touches the text and a text put keeps the fields. The write lands in the wiki's working layer (`wiki status` names it), or this face's personal layer of a wiki where it holds no writer's seat, and the receipt's `layer` names that placement; `bag` lands in that one bag through its store, under the gates its own writes keep. A seat's write aimed at a house canon bag refuses `seat-canon-reach`: a seat reaches canon through a recipe's copy-up and `meme_offer`. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

`base` carries the hash last read (a record's `hash`, a root's carrier `canonicalHash`; a slot read's partial base `partial:#/x:…` patches within its span and refuses `base-outside-span` beyond it): a record that moved past it answers `conflict`, naming the live hash, and nothing lands. A base guards honest reuse, never a lock. `create` lands only where no record stands, a family's root included; one standing answers `exists`.

`append` lands words at the end of the standing text with no base, read and written in one step on the live wiki, so two appends at once both land, in the order the record took them; a text that does not end on a newline takes one before the words. A terminal reads the words from a host path, or `-` for stdin; a seat names them. It names its words alone (`text`, `file`, `base`, `fields`, `unset` beside it refuse); `tag-add`, `tag-remove` and `create` ride beside it, and a missing title refuses unless `create` names it. Each call appends again.

`replace` names one exact span of the standing text and `with` the words it turns into (an empty `with` removes the span); the rest of the text never crosses the wire. The span counts as written, never trimmed, overlaps counted: zero refuses `replace-absent`, more than one `replace-ambiguous`, each naming the count and the read that cures it, and nothing moves. The result lands as a text put does, under the same base, and the receipt names `replaced`.

A meme family moves by the same put. A whole carrier as a root's text lands the family through the Confluence gate (the family re-splits and reseals; the answer adds `canonicalHash`, `landed`, `kept`, `tombstoned`); `slot` folds into the title (`<root>#/x`), so a slot's text lands with no base and an append honours the slot's standing postamble. Absence never deletes: a slot the new text omits stays standing by reference, named under `kept`, and `cut-slot` names each slot that leaves (a cut naming no standing omitted slot refuses `cut-not-omitted`). A family under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/<class>/<slug>` follows `stage-path-shape`.

The fences refuse by name: a family's `type` and carriage fields derive from its text (`family-carriage-derives`); a new slot joins through its parent's text (`family-joins-by-text`); a text the gate cannot read as one carrier refuses `family-gate-refused`; a title that stays home refuses `tiddler-withheld`; a put over a rendered tiddler, or one carrying `rendered-from`, refuses `rendered-derives`, since only the renderer writes it: edit the source records. Every other shape lands natively, a `$:/` title or tag, a module or plugin field and a script type alike. A put writes the face it wears and never another (`cross-face-write-refused`).

#/gate: read: a read asks the face's read cap on the anchor's working bag; a record another bag answers stays out where the face holds no read on it, and withheld counts it
#/head: one record or one meme, read on a gradient

Every record reads through this door, whatever its type: a plain note, a data tiddler, a meme's root or one of its slots. `recipe` names the wiki, and the read runs in that wiki's own TiddlyWiki engine: `default` names the worn face's daemon wiki, a slug any wiki this face reaches (one it hosts or one shared to it), and a wiki it reaches none of refuses `wiki-unreached`. `bag` names one bag and reads that bag's own record through its store, with no engine: the answer names the `bag`, and carries `floor: true` where the bag's floor snapshot answered. Exactly one of the two rides; a call that names neither reads `recipe/default`, the default the container row carries. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

Every answer leads with a `has` line: provenance (`recipe/` or `bag/`, `layer/`, `floor/true`), the record's own tags, its measures (`type/ position/ family/ slots/ bytes/ base/`, a pointer's `_canonical_uri/ textCid/ _integrity/ size/` verbatim), then the description or role; a meme's has-stack adds one line per slot. Beside it `grain` echoes {asked, applied, why} and `next` names the next unfold, or null.

Two axes ride apart. The lens: the record by default, {recipe or bag, title, lens: "record", tiddler: {fields, hash, textHash, bag, position, family?, omitted?}}, `tiddler` null where none stands; `meme` recomposes the root and its slot children into one carrier sealed by its block check, {title, lens: "meme", meme: {uri, text?, slotText?, canonicalHash, bytes, slots, slot?, page?}, withheld?}, and a record that holds no meme answers the record with a `note` saying so. The grain: none named, a record within one page (65536 bytes) answers fat and a longer one skinny, a pointer its handle; a meme within a page answers its whole carrier and a longer one its has-stack. `skinny` leaves the text home, `fat` carries it, `handle` names a pointer's body, `resolved` reads it from the local CAS by CID and verifies it (a web2 `_canonical_uri` stays named, never fetched), `slot` answers one slot's span at `meme.slotText`, and `whole` reads the whole at the lens's grain, a meme's carrier one page at a time, each page cut on a slot boundary: hand `next.after` back as `after` until `next` reads null; a terminal's `mu=assert` follows every page to the end and joins them. A call names the depth with `mu=relate` (the card) and `mu=assert` (the whole); the seat's own tool names `grain` until it folds into the call.

The text alone: a terminal's `form=text` writes the text's bytes to stdout and nothing else (the has line and the base go to stderr), a record's text whole with a pointer's body resolved, with `meme` the recomposed carrier, with `slot` that slot's span; an answer that carries no text refuses `text-unread` and names the read that cures it. A seat reads values, so the text already rides one named key per lens: `grain="whole"` answers a record's text at `tiddler.fields.text`, `mu=assert` the recomposed carrier at `meme.text`, and `meme` with `slot` one slot's span at `meme.slotText`.

Hand the answer's base to a write: a record's `hash`, a carrier's `canonicalHash`. An answer that left the text home hands a card's base (`skinny:sha256-…`): a field patch takes it, a text write refuses `base-from-skinny`, so read fat before you rewrite a text. A slot answer, or a page short of the end, hands a partial base bound to what it read (`partial:#/a:…`, `partial:p1:…`): a slot's put takes it within that span, a whole-carrier write or a family delete refuses `base-from-partial`, and the last page hands the bare base. A partial span guards honest base reuse and grants nothing.

With no title and `meme`, the door lists families: `tree` nests their slots and `after` names the next page. A bag listing answers {bag, roots, next}; a named recipe answers {recipe, bags, roots, next}; under `recipe="default"` no row names a `bag`. A floor read answers {bag, floor, roots, next}, and each row from a recipe's floor bag carries `floor: true`.

A rendered tiddler answers whole here: a source marked `projection: rendered` derives a live tiddler (`<source>.rendered`, or the source's `render-title`) whose `rendered-from` names the source. `fields` answers the named fields alone; `max-bytes` caps a record answer, the largest fields leaving first, named under `omitted`. `target` names another lit face this read visits, by handle index or pet name, while the call keeps the face it wears: a visit reads that face's daemon wiki through its canon and working layer, never its personal or draft layer (`cross-face-private`), and a shut face refuses `face-not-open`. A record's text carries the words of the layer that answered; turn it through the five tools.

lares get — read one record or meme by title, on a gradient, from a wiki or bag
one record or one meme, read on a gradient

Every record reads through this door, whatever its type: a plain note, a data tiddler, a meme's root or one of its slots. `recipe` names the wiki, and the read runs in that wiki's own TiddlyWiki engine: `default` names the worn face's daemon wiki, a slug any wiki this face reaches (one it hosts or one shared to it), and a wiki it reaches none of refuses `wiki-unreached`. `bag` names one bag and reads that bag's own record through its store, with no engine: the answer names the `bag`, and carries `floor: true` where the bag's floor snapshot answered. Exactly one of the two rides; a call that names neither reads `recipe/default`, the default the container row carries. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

Every answer leads with a `has` line: provenance (`recipe/` or `bag/`, `layer/`, `floor/true`), the record's own tags, its measures (`type/ position/ family/ slots/ bytes/ base/`, a pointer's `_canonical_uri/ textCid/ _integrity/ size/` verbatim), then the description or role; a meme's has-stack adds one line per slot. Beside it `grain` echoes {asked, applied, why} and `next` names the next unfold, or null.

Two axes ride apart. The lens: the record by default, {recipe or bag, title, lens: "record", tiddler: {fields, hash, textHash, bag, position, family?, omitted?}}, `tiddler` null where none stands; `meme` recomposes the root and its slot children into one carrier sealed by its block check, {title, lens: "meme", meme: {uri, text?, slotText?, canonicalHash, bytes, slots, slot?, page?}, withheld?}, and a record that holds no meme answers the record with a `note` saying so. The grain: none named, a record within one page (65536 bytes) answers fat and a longer one skinny, a pointer its handle; a meme within a page answers its whole carrier and a longer one its has-stack. `skinny` leaves the text home, `fat` carries it, `handle` names a pointer's body, `resolved` reads it from the local CAS by CID and verifies it (a web2 `_canonical_uri` stays named, never fetched), `slot` answers one slot's span at `meme.slotText`, and `whole` reads the whole at the lens's grain, a meme's carrier one page at a time, each page cut on a slot boundary: hand `next.after` back as `after` until `next` reads null; a terminal's `mu=assert` follows every page to the end and joins them. A call names the depth with `mu=relate` (the card) and `mu=assert` (the whole); the seat's own tool names `grain` until it folds into the call.

The text alone: a terminal's `form=text` writes the text's bytes to stdout and nothing else (the has line and the base go to stderr), a record's text whole with a pointer's body resolved, with `meme` the recomposed carrier, with `slot` that slot's span; an answer that carries no text refuses `text-unread` and names the read that cures it. A seat reads values, so the text already rides one named key per lens: `grain="whole"` answers a record's text at `tiddler.fields.text`, `mu=assert` the recomposed carrier at `meme.text`, and `meme` with `slot` one slot's span at `meme.slotText`.

Hand the answer's base to a write: a record's `hash`, a carrier's `canonicalHash`. An answer that left the text home hands a card's base (`skinny:sha256-…`): a field patch takes it, a text write refuses `base-from-skinny`, so read fat before you rewrite a text. A slot answer, or a page short of the end, hands a partial base bound to what it read (`partial:#/a:…`, `partial:p1:…`): a slot's put takes it within that span, a whole-carrier write or a family delete refuses `base-from-partial`, and the last page hands the bare base. A partial span guards honest base reuse and grants nothing.

With no title and `meme`, the door lists families: `tree` nests their slots and `after` names the next page. A bag listing answers {bag, roots, next}; a named recipe answers {recipe, bags, roots, next}; under `recipe="default"` no row names a `bag`. A floor read answers {bag, floor, roots, next}, and each row from a recipe's floor bag carries `floor: true`.

A rendered tiddler answers whole here: a source marked `projection: rendered` derives a live tiddler (`<source>.rendered`, or the source's `render-title`) whose `rendered-from` names the source. `fields` answers the named fields alone; `max-bytes` caps a record answer, the largest fields leaving first, named under `omitted`. `target` names another lit face this read visits, by handle index or pet name, while the call keeps the face it wears: a visit reads that face's daemon wiki through its canon and working layer, never its personal or draft layer (`cross-face-private`), and a shut face refuses `face-not-open`. A record's text carries the words of the layer that answered; turn it through the five tools.
Examples:
lares get 'title=Room 4' recipe=default    # the record on its gradient, fat within a page; the base rides beside it
lares get title=lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/api/pono/affordance recipe=lares mu=relate    # the card at mu relate: the has-stack, one line per slot
lares get title=lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/api/pono/affordance recipe=lares mu=assert 'slot=#/takes'    # the whole at mu assert, slot narrowing it to one span
lares get 'title=Room 4' mu=relate    # every field, the text left home
lares get 'title=Room 4' bag=lares    # that one bag's record, its base and the bag that answered
lares get title=lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/api/pono/affordance recipe=lares meme=true 'slot=#/takes'    # one slot of a meme, its partial base beside it
lares get title=lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/api/pono/affordance recipe=lares mu=assert    # the whole carrier, paged on slot boundaries and joined
lares get 'title=Room 4' form=text    # the text alone on stdout, ready for a pipe; the has line and base on stderr
lares get recipe=default meme=true tree=true    # the family roots this view holds, each with its slots

whole: Read one record or meme by title, on a gradient, from a wiki or bag

Every record reads through this door, whatever its type: a plain note, a data tiddler, a meme's root or one of its slots. `recipe` names the wiki, and the read runs in that wiki's own TiddlyWiki engine: `default` names the worn face's daemon wiki, a slug any wiki this face reaches (one it hosts or one shared to it), and a wiki it reaches none of refuses `wiki-unreached`. `bag` names one bag and reads that bag's own record through its store, with no engine: the answer names the `bag`, and carries `floor: true` where the bag's floor snapshot answered. Exactly one of the two rides; a call that names neither reads `recipe/default`, the default the container row carries. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

Every answer leads with a `has` line: provenance (`recipe/` or `bag/`, `layer/`, `floor/true`), the record's own tags, its measures (`type/ position/ family/ slots/ bytes/ base/`, a pointer's `_canonical_uri/ textCid/ _integrity/ size/` verbatim), then the description or role; a meme's has-stack adds one line per slot. Beside it `grain` echoes {asked, applied, why} and `next` names the next unfold, or null.

Two axes ride apart. The lens: the record by default, {recipe or bag, title, lens: "record", tiddler: {fields, hash, textHash, bag, position, family?, omitted?}}, `tiddler` null where none stands; `meme` recomposes the root and its slot children into one carrier sealed by its block check, {title, lens: "meme", meme: {uri, text?, slotText?, canonicalHash, bytes, slots, slot?, page?}, withheld?}, and a record that holds no meme answers the record with a `note` saying so. The grain: none named, a record within one page (65536 bytes) answers fat and a longer one skinny, a pointer its handle; a meme within a page answers its whole carrier and a longer one its has-stack. `skinny` leaves the text home, `fat` carries it, `handle` names a pointer's body, `resolved` reads it from the local CAS by CID and verifies it (a web2 `_canonical_uri` stays named, never fetched), `slot` answers one slot's span at `meme.slotText`, and `whole` reads the whole at the lens's grain, a meme's carrier one page at a time, each page cut on a slot boundary: hand `next.after` back as `after` until `next` reads null; a terminal's `mu=assert` follows every page to the end and joins them. A call names the depth with `mu=relate` (the card) and `mu=assert` (the whole); the seat's own tool names `grain` until it folds into the call.

The text alone: a terminal's `form=text` writes the text's bytes to stdout and nothing else (the has line and the base go to stderr), a record's text whole with a pointer's body resolved, with `meme` the recomposed carrier, with `slot` that slot's span; an answer that carries no text refuses `text-unread` and names the read that cures it. Hand the answer's base to a write: a record's `hash`, a carrier's `canonicalHash`. An answer that left the text home hands a card's base (`skinny:sha256-…`): a field patch takes it, a text write refuses `base-from-skinny`, so read fat before you rewrite a text. A slot answer, or a page short of the end, hands a partial base bound to what it read (`partial:#/a:…`, `partial:p1:…`): a slot's put takes it within that span, a whole-carrier write or a family delete refuses `base-from-partial`, and the last page hands the bare base. A partial span guards honest base reuse and grants nothing.

With no title and `meme`, the door lists families: `tree` nests their slots and `after` names the next page. A bag listing answers {bag, roots, next}; a named recipe answers {recipe, bags, roots, next}; under `recipe="default"` no row names a `bag`. A floor read answers {bag, floor, roots, next}, and each row from a recipe's floor bag carries `floor: true`.

A rendered tiddler answers whole here: a source marked `projection: rendered` derives a live tiddler (`<source>.rendered`, or the source's `render-title`) whose `rendered-from` names the source. `fields` answers the named fields alone; `max-bytes` caps a record answer, the largest fields leaving first, named under `omitted`. `target` names another lit face this read visits, by handle index or pet name, while the call keeps the face it wears: a visit reads that face's daemon wiki through its canon and working layer, never its personal or draft layer (`cross-face-private`), and a shut face refuses `face-not-open`. A record's text carries the words of the layer that answered; turn it through the five tools.

#/answers: removed (exit 0)  the act landed; mode reads plain, kapae, reveal or cut
absent (exit 3)  nothing stood to remove
refused (exit 4)  the family law or a lower layer refused; the consequence rides the answer and nothing moved

dry (exit 0)  a dry delete: the answer the real delete would give, the base it needs and the carrier's seat hints; nothing landed
#/gate: write: the Kahu predicate, then the face's write cap on each layer the consequence writes
#/head: a delete by the family law, plain unless a lower layer makes it a choice

A delete deletes plainly: with no `mode`, each record leaves its own layer to absent and no tombstone rises (the receipt reads `mode: "plain"` and names each title under `retracted`). `base` carries the hash last read: a record that moved past it moves nothing and answers `conflict`, naming the live hash. A title the wiki reads absent answers `absent`, and a plain delete there retracts a kāpae that hides nothing (its `.kapae` shadow leaves the disk). The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The family law decides what moves, read over the reader's view before anything lands. A plain tiddler leaves alone. A meme root answers the consequence the delete would land (every title it would move, what it would leave) and refuses `tiddler-delete-in-a-family` unless `family` names the family act, which lands the root and its slots as one change per layer (the answer adds `canonicalHash`). A slot's title (`<root>#/x`) leaves as the explicit cut on its parent, and the family reseals.

Only a lower layer makes a delete a choice. A wiki composes layers (canon under working under personal), and one title may stand in several. Where a lower layer holds the title too, or the record rests in a layer this face cannot remove it from, a delete naming no mode refuses `delete-mode-needed` and names both meanings: `mode` kapae raises a tombstone in a writable layer that shadows every record beneath (the wiki reads the title gone, the lower layers keep theirs); `mode` reveal retracts the topmost record so the one beneath surfaces, refusing `reveal-top-unwritable` where the face cannot write that layer. Each act in `consequence.acts` names `bag` (the layer written), `holds` (every layer holding the title) and what the wiki reads afterward: `shadowed: [bags]` or `reveals: bag | null`.

A rendered tiddler (one carrying `rendered-from`) refuses `rendered-derives`: only the renderer writes it, and it leaves when its source drops `projection: rendered`. A `$:/` title refuses too. `recipe` removes through that wiki's engine; `bag` removes from that one bag through its store, `family` taking the family there too. A delete writes the face it wears and never another (`cross-face-write-refused`).

lares delete — remove one record, or a meme family by name, from a wiki or bag
a delete by the family law, plain unless a lower layer makes it a choice

A delete deletes plainly: with no `mode`, each record leaves its own layer to absent and no tombstone rises (the receipt reads `mode: "plain"` and names each title under `retracted`). `base` carries the hash last read: a record that moved past it moves nothing and answers `conflict`, naming the live hash. A title the wiki reads absent answers `absent`, and a plain delete there retracts a kāpae that hides nothing (its `.kapae` shadow leaves the disk). The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The family law decides what moves, read over the reader's view before anything lands. A plain tiddler leaves alone. A meme root answers the consequence the delete would land (every title it would move, what it would leave) and refuses `tiddler-delete-in-a-family` unless `family` names the family act, which lands the root and its slots as one change per layer (the answer adds `canonicalHash`). A slot's title (`<root>#/x`) leaves as the explicit cut on its parent, and the family reseals.

Only a lower layer makes a delete a choice. A wiki composes layers (canon under working under personal), and one title may stand in several. Where a lower layer holds the title too, or the record rests in a layer this face cannot remove it from, a delete naming no mode refuses `delete-mode-needed` and names both meanings: `mode` kapae raises a tombstone in a writable layer that shadows every record beneath (the wiki reads the title gone, the lower layers keep theirs); `mode` reveal retracts the topmost record so the one beneath surfaces, refusing `reveal-top-unwritable` where the face cannot write that layer. Each act in `consequence.acts` names `bag` (the layer written), `holds` (every layer holding the title) and what the wiki reads afterward: `shadowed: [bags]` or `reveals: bag | null`.

A rendered tiddler (one carrying `rendered-from`) refuses `rendered-derives`: only the renderer writes it, and it leaves when its source drops `projection: rendered`. A `$:/` title refuses too. `recipe` removes through that wiki's engine; `bag` removes from that one bag through its store, `family` taking the family there too. A delete writes the face it wears and never another (`cross-face-write-refused`).
Examples:
lares delete 'title=Old Note' recipe=default 'base=<hash>'    # the record leaves; a stale base moves nothing
lares delete title=lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/x recipe=default family=true    # a meme root and its slots, one change
lares delete 'title=Room 4' recipe=default mode=reveal    # drop my copy; the layer beneath surfaces
lares delete 'title=Room 4' recipe=default mode=kapae    # hide the title; the layers beneath keep theirs
lares delete 'title=Old Note' bag=notes    # that one bag's record leaves through its store

whole: engine.record.renames(title=<title>, to=<title>, recipe=<slug>, [base=<hash>], [face=<handle>])
— move one record to a new title; references follow, the old one forwards
a move over TiddlyWiki's own relink, the old title left as a forwarder

A rename moves one record (a meme root takes its slots along) over TiddlyWiki's own relink: every reference the engine's relinkers rewrite follows (the core relinks tags and list fields; wikitext links follow only where a relink plugin mounts), and the old title stays as a forwarder, a pointer tiddler (`forward-to`) whose text transcludes the new one, so old roads keep answering. The address stays a candidate until the operator reads the landing's list.

The move runs in one wiki's engine and lands in its working layer alone, so it names a `recipe` and never a bag (`wiki-not-anchored`). A record resting in another layer (or one the shore still carries, with no layer named yet) refuses `rename-source-layer`; referrers outside the working layer refuse `rename-referrers-unreachable`, a count and never titles; a standing target refuses `rename-target-stands` and names the delete that clears it; a slot refuses `slot-without-root` and names its root; a `lar:` title another layer holds too takes a hand alone. A `$:/` title on either side refuses `rename-system-title`, since a forwarder would answer as the setting: put the new title, then delete the standing one.

An answer names only records this face reads and counts the rest (`withheld`); a referrer that stays home keeps its fields (`skipped`). `base` carries the hash last read: a record that moved past it answers `conflict` and nothing moves.
Examples:
<$ title="Room 4" to="Room Four" recipe="default"/>    # references follow; the old title stays as a forwarder
<$ title="Room 4" to="Room Four" recipe="default" base="<hash>"/>    # a stale base moves nothing

to <title>  the title it moves to
recipe <slug>  the wiki whose engine relinks; default names the worn face's daemon wiki
base <hash>  the hash last read; a stale one answers conflict and nothing moves
face <handle>  the lit face this call wears, by handle or pet name

rename-source-layer  the record rests in a layer other than the working one; the move lands in the working layer alone
rename-referrers-unreachable  referrers outside the working layer cannot follow; the answer counts them and names none

Without `--wait` it returns the matching entries already standing, within a ten-second read; with `--wait` it holds (up to two minutes) and answers on the first matching entry after `--since`, or after now where `--since` is absent. The cursor reads `<epoch:writer:seq>`, the seq a whole number from 1; the one kind today is `bag-projected`. Without a vessel standing the verb refuses by name and carries its hint.
`--json` prints the structured payload; the human line reads `events: N`, then one JSON line per entry.
Gate (the carrier's testimony; the door checks): read: a read of the journal through the daemon; it writes nothing.
Refuses: unknown-kind · invalid-since · daemon-unreachable.
Answers band: listed · refused.
Mirrors: lares events (affordance engine.status.follows).

After a root rotation the earlier items read in history alone until the operator's hand carries them: `kahua carry <cid>…` names the revision cids that keep standing, or `--all` names every earlier head the history reads (never both). One root-signed act at the current epoch stands them again. It runs on a person's hand alone, and no tool carries it. Every answer prints as JSON.

Under a pūlama the root signs at the pūlama's hand door, since the vessel there holds no face root: `--terms` runs every gate and prints ONE stdout line (the one unsigned act its root signs) and opens no route; the pūlama's `sign '<terms>'` checks it and signs; `--land '<answer>'` lands the signed record, where the door builds the act afresh and lands it only over a byte-equal body. Neither asks the passphrase on the vessel, and the host shim walks the pattern (`tools/lares-container.sh kahua lift|withdraw|carry`).

params.proposals: the batch: a list of {title, revision, text | digest, taint}, never empty (a JSON list on the terminal)
params.session: the seat session the call rides; absent, the tool's own

#/answers: proposed (exit 0)  the batch landed on the face's intents plane; the id names it for a lift's --proposal
#/gate: seat-or-hand: a proposal grants nothing: the operator's signed lift decides; it rides the face's intents plane pinned to this device, and a seat session proposes as the hand does
#/head: a seat proposes one batch; the operator's hand lifts

`proposals` lists {title, revision, text | digest, taint}: the daemon title and revision the item distils, its body (or the body's sha-256 digest) and every input from outside the face (a web page, tool output, pasted text); an AI summary inherits the taint of what it summarised. ONE batch per call rides the face's intents plane, pinned to this device; it carries digests and never a body, and it GRANTS NOTHING: the operator's hand lifts it with `lares kahua lift <title> --proposal <id>`.

TWO DIGESTS, ONE WORD. A proposal's `digest` names the BODY digest, the sha-256 of the raw body bytes (UTF-8, lowercase hex); the seat's tool computes it from `text`. The ROW digest that `kahua stage` prints and `lift --digest` takes covers the body AND the row's carried fields, so it differs. Hand `text`, or the BODY digest; a proposal built from the ROW digest refuses at the lift with `proposal-digest`, as does one whose body differs by a byte from the staged row's.

Any seat proposes. The seat's tool rides a local `seat` session over the @daemon wire, whose profile the vessel refuses every kahua pin, lift, withdraw and carry; no tool lifts (`face.draft.stages` writes the local row a lift names). Returns {id, cid}.
#/refuses: kahua-proposal-proposals  name proposals as a non-empty list of {title, revision, text | digest, taint}
cure: lares kahua propose --proposals <proposals>
proposals-malformed  --proposals needs JSON
cure: lares kahua propose --proposals <proposals>
face-not-lent  the face stands outside the lent set the seat may name
face-not-open  the face stands shut; open it first
proposal-digest  at the lift: a proposal built from the row digest, or whose body differs by a byte from the staged row's, refuses there

#/answers: lifted (exit 0)  the row lifted under the face's root; the door's answer prints as JSON
landed-nothing (exit 0)  a head already carries the row; nothing landed
refused (exit 1)  the door refused by name; the line carries its reason
#/gate: hand: signs under the face's root out of sealed custody and always asks the face's passphrase at a terminal; a person runs it, an AI seat proposes and stages and names the command, and a bare --yes lifts nothing
#/head: the hand reads the preview, names the row digest, and the lift signs

`kahua lift <title>` carries one staged row to every device the face wears: the second crossing of memory. It reads the staged row back first and prints its PREVIEW (title, row digest, fields, body, and whether a head already carries it), then lifts only on that row digest typed back at a terminal (its first eight hex), or on `--digest <hex>` naming the digest the preview printed. A bare `--yes` names no digest and lifts nothing. A lift signs under the face's root, so a lift always asks the face's passphrase at a terminal; `--digest` spares the typed-back digest alone.

The lift names its taint list: `--taint none` when every input came from inside the face, else `--taint a,b`. A lift carries the staged row's own body and fields, so stage them first (`face.draft.stages`); a lift naming `--text`, `--file` or `--fields` refuses `kahua-lift-unstaged`. `--parent <cid>` names the revision it supersedes (`none` for a first lift), `--sources` further daemon sources the item distils (the staged row always rides), and `--proposal <id>` the proposal it answers: the proposal's body digest must equal the staged body's. Two digests share one word: the ROW digest (what `kahua stage` answers and a lift names) covers the row's body and fields, while a proposal's `digest` names the BODY digest, the body bytes alone.

— lift one staged row by title and digest, signed under the face's root
the hand reads the preview, names the row digest, and the lift signs

`kahua lift <title>` carries one staged row to every device the face wears: the second crossing of memory. It reads the staged row back first and prints its PREVIEW (title, row digest, fields, body, and whether a head already carries it), then lifts only on that row digest typed back at a terminal (its first eight hex), or on `--digest <hex>` naming the digest the preview printed. A bare `--yes` names no digest and lifts nothing. A lift signs under the face's root, so a lift always asks the face's passphrase at a terminal; `--digest` spares the typed-back digest alone.

The lift names its taint list: `--taint none` when every input came from inside the face, else `--taint a,b`. A lift carries the staged row's own body and fields, so stage them first (`face.draft.stages`); a lift naming `--text`, `--file` or `--fields` refuses `kahua-lift-unstaged`. `--parent <cid>` names the revision it supersedes (`none` for a first lift), `--sources` further daemon sources the item distils (the staged row always rides), and `--proposal <id>` the proposal it answers: the proposal's body digest must equal the staged body's. Two digests share one word: the ROW digest (what `kahua stage` answers and a lift names) covers the row's body and fields, while a proposal's `digest` names the BODY digest, the body bytes alone.

The door re-reads the row at the act and refuses `kahua-lift-unstaged` (no such row) or `kahua-lift-digest-moved` (the row moved since the preview); a lift the head already carries lands nothing. The lift reads the lōkahi cap off the vessel's island and the operator's grant out of sealed custody, and refuses by name; an AI seat proposes and stages, and its session never lifts. `lares shore lift-kahua` lifts a different thing, the pending set a lay left behind (`carriage.draft.lifts`).

Under a pūlama the root signs at the pūlama's hand door, since the vessel there holds no face root: `--terms` runs every gate and prints ONE stdout line (the one unsigned act its root signs) and opens no route; the pūlama's `sign '<terms>'` checks it and signs; `--land '<answer>'` lands the signed record, where the door builds the act afresh and lands it only over a byte-equal body. Neither asks the passphrase on the vessel, and the host shim walks the pattern (`tools/lares-container.sh kahua lift|withdraw|carry`).

<$ title="T" taint="none" face="1" terms="yes"/>    # print the one terms line a pūlama signs, opening no route

The house consults an oracle whose corpus rests on a library shelf (`lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/library/oracles/<kind>/`). The kind rides as data: `by` names the shelf (the E-Jing by default), and the shelf's index record declares its own `method`, its corpus and its credits. The e-jing and doa shelves declare `three-coins`: the I Ching by three coins a line (heads three, tails two: 6 old yin and 9 old yang change, 7 and 8 hold). A new oracle joins as a shelf, never a new address or a new verb; a shelf whose method the verb runs not yet refuses by name.

Every consult lands once, as a meme under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/oracle/casts/`, whose five slots run OODA-HA (`#/loop`), whatever the kind. The ask fills `#/observe` with its context pointers and `#/orient` with its gathered uncertainty and its query; the house fills `#/decide` with the throw and every reading the wiki holds, each source credited; the seat appends its reading, its move and its aftermath by slot append. The verb reads the loop's shape from the carrier the caller's stack seats for this address (a carrier a working layer seats above canon shapes the act in its place), the affordance pack its binary baked standing as the floor, and the answer names the carrier slot that shaped it. One asking, one throw: the same query by the same booked asker answers the standing cast and names the uncertainty it kept. The coins draw through the platform's entropy door, or a person types the six values thrown with real coins. The verb reads no clock: the caller names the time as testimony. A weak seed reads back: the record names a seed by a 16-hex digest anyone can test a guess against, so a person choosing one chooses a strong one.
The cast stands as a blind throw to collide uncertainty with: the throw stands, the reading stays open.

The house consults an oracle whose corpus rests on a library shelf (`lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/library/oracles/<kind>/`). The kind rides as data: `by` names the shelf (the E-Jing by default), and the shelf's index record declares its own `method`, its corpus and its credits. The e-jing and doa shelves declare `three-coins`: the I Ching by three coins a line (heads three, tails two: 6 old yin and 9 old yang change, 7 and 8 hold). A new oracle joins as a shelf, never a new address or a new verb; a shelf whose method the verb runs not yet refuses by name.

Every consult lands once, as a meme under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/oracle/casts/`, whose five slots run OODA-HA (`#/loop`), whatever the kind. The ask fills `#/observe` with its context pointers and `#/orient` with its gathered uncertainty and its query; the house fills `#/decide` with the throw and every reading the wiki holds, each source credited; the seat appends its reading, its move and its aftermath by slot append. The verb reads the loop's shape from the carrier the caller's stack seats for this address (a carrier a working layer seats above canon shapes the act in its place), the affordance pack its binary baked standing as the floor, and the answer names the carrier slot that shaped it. One asking, one throw: the same query by the same booked asker answers the standing cast and names the uncertainty it kept. The coins draw through the platform's entropy door, or a person types the six values thrown with real coins. The verb reads no clock: the caller names the time as testimony. A weak seed reads back: the record names a seed by a 16-hex digest anyone can test a guess against, so a person choosing one chooses a strong one.
The cast stands as a blind throw to collide uncertainty with: the throw stands, the reading stays open.

The house computes the day in the Discordian calendar with its own isomorphic core, so a machine with no host `ddate` binary (a vessel's container, a bare host) reads it all the same. Five seasons of 73 days (Chaos, Discord, Confusion, Bureaucracy, The Aftermath) run a five-day week (Sweetmorn, Boomtime, Pungenday, Prickle-Prickle, Setting Orange); the YOLD runs the Gregorian year plus 1166; St. Tib's Day falls on February 29 with no season and no weekday; an apostle's holyday falls on day 5 of a season and its season holyday on day 50.

#/gate: hand: a share lands a grant from the owner's hive; a person runs the landing at their own terminal, and an AI harness on its branch refuses by name

A share row says who reads and who writes a bag, by face PET-NAME as a title list (`a b [[c d]]`), `*` for every face, or empty; `hN` and `--face N` resolve to that face's pet-name (`--face` adds face N to the readers), so a row always names faces by pet-name. A line names its DELTA: `--read` and `--write` add names beside the standing ones and never replace a list, `--read-remove` and `--write-remove` take names out (each taken-out face's landed grant revokes; a face standing shut keeps the row as it stood, named), and what the line leaves unnamed (the other list, the note, the owner) stands, so the same line twice changes nothing. `--list` shows every row and the one resolver's answer per bag (with `--json`, each row AS WRITTEN beside the resolver's answer); `--remove` unshares the row.

The row writes through to `$LAR_ROOT/config/share.tid` (it survives a re-founding; a person edits it by hand, and the next boot reconciles it in, the file winning) and, with a vessel standing, into the control document (`share-set`); then the operator's hand lands it (`share-apply`): each lit grantee takes the bag's row by reference and a delegation from the owner's hive, and a grant whose face stands shut waits behind an opaque flag until it lights. ONE ROW PER SLUG: a wiki row standing for the slug refuses `share-kind-standing`, and nothing writes. Sharing rides by reference and delegation, never a copy.

cli: lares kapae flag <digest> --why 'the macro reads a file it should not'

params.digest: the promoted item's digest, 64 lowercase hex
params.drop: read by no kapae act: the trust door's orphan decision names it, and a kapae line ignores it
params.face: which face's promotion plane this call reads or acts on, by persona index (a whole number from 0)
params.keep: read by no kapae act: the trust door's orphan decision names it, and a kapae line ignores it
params.why: the reason the brake should rise
params.wiki: the wiki the promotion belongs to; absent, the daemon wiki

#/answers: flagged (exit 0)  the flag stands on the board; the answer prints as JSON
#/gate: seat-or-hand: a flag grants nothing: the hand's raise decides
#/head: the AI flags with a reason; the hand raises

Every wiki wears promotion capability; its edge holds (face, wiki, digest). The AI prepares and flags; the hand commits and raises. The brake sets one promoted item aside by a signed marker, and a lower takes the marker down. The wiki rides `--wiki` (absent: the daemon wiki), the face `--face N`, and every answer prints as JSON. The word names five doors in the house: the nexus quorum ban (`lares nexus kapae`) and a relation's marker (`lares edge kapae`) stay beside it, the seat's branch mute reads at `sense.kapae.mutes`, and a record's tombstone rides `lares delete`.
`kapae flag <digest> --why <reason>` puts a flag on the board for an item, found among the waiting items or the carried rows; it raises nothing. The reason rides the flag.

cure: lares kapae flag <digest> --why <reason>

The hook-lever stands on its own: a marker file a capture hook checks and steps aside on when present (whatever runs the `lares sense capture` and `lares sense telemetry` legs on a session event). A migration or a `lares sense teardown` then runs WITHOUT daemon-spawn contention: the minting stops at the source, with no whack-a-mole against spawned children. `lares mempalace quiesce` pauses AND drains the warm daemons in one gesture; this lever suppresses minting alone, touching no live daemon.

`hooks pause [--reason <t>]` writes the marker (the reason defaults to `manual`) and answers {wasPaused, hooksPaused, marker, since, reason}; pausing again refreshes the reason. Run `lares mempalace quiesce` to drain the warm daemons, and `hooks resume` to un-pause.

lares hooks pause --reason migrate    # pause and record why

ddate.brief: read the Discordian date from the house's own calendar; no vessel
help: usage: lares ddate [+FORMAT] [<day> <month> <year>]
lares ddate — read the Discordian date from the house's own calendar; no vessel
the day in the Discordian calendar, from the house's own core

The house computes the day in the Discordian calendar with its own isomorphic core, so a machine with no host `ddate` binary (a vessel's container, a bare host) reads it all the same. Five seasons of 73 days (Chaos, Discord, Confusion, Bureaucracy, The Aftermath) run a five-day week (Sweetmorn, Boomtime, Pungenday, Prickle-Prickle, Setting Orange); the YOLD runs the Gregorian year plus 1166; St. Tib's Day falls on February 29 with no season and no weekday; an apostle's holyday falls on day 5 of a season and its season holyday on day 50.

With no date the verb reads today's local day: the command and the seat each read the clock once, at the caller's side of the seam, and hand the day to the core, which reads none. The `day`, `month` and `year` ride together or not at all (a BCE year rides negative), and a date out of range refuses. X-Day (Confusion 40, 9827 YOLD) stands as the Church of the SubGenius's date, moved forward once the first X-Day passed without incident; `%X` counts the days to it.

Format codes follow ddate(1), with `%E` added: `%A %a` weekday, long and short · `%B %b` season, long and short · `%d` day of the season · `%e` the ordinal (1st, 11th, 21st, 22nd, 23rd) · `%E` the ordinal by its last digit alone (11st, 12nd, 13rd), the first ddate's reading, an easter egg · `%H` the day's holyday, if any · `%N` stop here unless the day holds a holyday · `%Y` the YOLD · `%X` days until X-Day (negative once it passed) · `%n %t` newline, tab · `%.` an exclamation from the platform's entropy door (crypto.getRandomValues) · `%{ %}` the span between them reads "St. Tib's Day" on February 29 and prints plain on every other day.

A bare call answers the default line ("Today is Prickle-Prickle, the 32nd day of The Aftermath in the YOLD 3192"). On a terminal that line prints plain, like ddate(1), and `--json` answers the envelope the seat always returns: {text, entropy, gregorian, yold, tibs, season, dayOfSeason, weekday, holyday}, where `entropy` names the source a `%.` drew from, else null. The verb runs on the host and needs no vessel; the MCP tool rides the @daemon wire.
Examples:
lares ddate    # today, with the default format
lares ddate 5 1 2024    # a named day: Setting Orange, Chaos 5, 3190 YOLD
lares ddate '+%{%A, the %e of %B%}, %Y. %N%nCelebrate %H' 19 2 2025    # a format over a named day, the holyday line only on a holyday
lares ddate '+%X' 20 11 2026    # days until X-Day
lares ddate '+%. %E'    # an exclamation and the first ddate's ordinal
Flags:
+FORMAT  the ddate(1) format codes the head lists; absent, the default line
<day>  the day of the month; day, month and year ride together or not at all
<month>  the month, 1 to 12; rides with day and year
<year>  the Gregorian year (a BCE year rides negative); rides with day and month
Gate (the carrier's testimony; the door checks):
host: runs on the host and needs no vessel, no house root and no key
clock: the caller names the day: with no date the command or the seat reads its own local calendar day once and hands it to the core, which reads no clock
Refuses (each with its cure):
usage  a malformed line (usage: ddate [+format] [day month year]); the human render prints the help lines and the code reads usage
cure: lares ddate 5 1 2024
date-out-of-range  Invalid date -- out of range; the code reads usage and the MCP tool raises
cure: lares ddate 19 2 2025

ingest.brief: scan disk into records through the Confluence gate
help: usage: lares ingest --source <dir-or-file> --to <bag-uri> [--apply] [--tag-blobs] [--in-wiki] [--change-id <id>] [--watch] [--debounce <ms>]
lares ingest — scan disk into records through the Confluence gate
the disk-to-records gesture: scan, diff, preview, then apply through the gate

The gesture holds the disk grant and the Synced tree (the island holds neither; readiness reads local on both sides of the shore). It scans the source for `.mem` carriers, derives each address by the address-siting rule, and diffs the disk hash against the synced hash per carrier. The default posture PREVIEWS: it prints NEW, UNCHANGED and CHANGED rows and submits nothing. `--apply` sends the NEW and CHANGED carriers, their hashes riding an INGEST verb, and the island runs the full Confluence gate (its currentRenderHash stands as the third leg) and answers per carrier.

`--tag-blobs` stamps the CAS opt-in flag (a `.meta` sidecar, or a meme's ahu meta) on the large un-flagged carriers that would fault during LOAD or INGEST; it writes no records, and the preview names the count. `--watch` fires the same gesture per settled wave instead of once: one wave per quiet window (`--debounce` ms), preview by default, `--apply` submits. A file that vanished tombstones nothing: the watcher hands it to the vessel's shore, where it stands pending until a person answers with `lares shore remove` or `lares shore restore`. A file that holds no base never lands over records that say something else, and a file that moved while the records moved never lands: each stands off at the vessel's shore (`lares shore`), and every wave says no person stands behind it (`unattended`). `--in-wiki` runs the INGEST in the active wiki's island, the path for the working write-layer ingest-back (a `wikis/` source derives its URIs off that layer).

The one-shot flags (`--yes`, `--tag-blobs`, `--in-wiki`, `--change-id`) ride the one-shot ingest and refuse beside `--watch`; `--debounce` rides `--watch` alone. A scan that skipped every carrier answers usage and names the mirror directories it derived against, since the source must sit under the bags dir (LAR_BAGS) or wikis dir (LAR_WIKIS) as `<holding>/<w.w.w>/…/<name>.<ext>`.
Examples:
lares ingest --source ./bags/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares    # scan and diff; submit nothing
lares ingest --source ./bags/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares --apply    # send the new and changed carriers through the gate
lares ingest --source ./bags/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares --tag-blobs    # flag the large carriers that would fault during ingest
lares ingest --source ./bags/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/bags/lares --watch --debounce 500    # fire one preview wave per quiet window of 500 ms
lares ingest --source ./wikis/lares --to lar:///ha.ka.ba/wikis/lares/working --in-wiki --apply    # ingest a working-layer mirror back through the wiki's island

--source <dir-or-file>  the disk source to scan: a directory or one file under the bags or wikis mirror tree
--to <bag-uri>  the bag the carriers land in
--apply  send the new and changed carriers through the island's INGEST gate; absent, a preview
--tag-blobs  write the CAS opt-in flag for the large un-flagged carriers; writes no records
--in-wiki  run the INGEST in the active wiki's island
--change-id <id>  the wave's own change identity; absent, the verb mints one
--watch  fire the gesture per settled wave instead of once
--debounce <ms>  the watcher's quiet window in milliseconds; rides --watch alone

mcp.brief: hold an MCP client's seat steady while the surface falls and rises
help: usage: lares mcp aho [[-- <child argv…>]]

the aho: the client never sees a respawn

`lares mcp aho` holds an MCP client's stdio for the session's whole life and spawns the house's own surface as a child that may fall and rise, resolved again at each spawn (the container's seat where the container house stands, else the native one); `lares mcp aho -- <child argv…>` names another child (a test, another surface), and everything after `--` rides to it as written, flags and all. While no child stands the seat answers `initialize` and the tool list from what the child last answered, replays the handshake to each new child itself, and answers a call at once with the tool error `hearth-sleeps`. A call in flight at a child's death answers `outcome-unknown: re-read before re-trying`, and the seat never sends it again. It sends one `list_changed` when a new child lists other tools. It logs event names and counts alone and holds no key.

A harness config records `lares mcp aho` and nothing beneath it (`lares home tend` writes that entry), so what stands under the verb may change with no config rewritten. The committed bin runs this seat before it loads the dispatcher, so the seat a harness spawns loads no custody, no vessel and no house root.

oracle.brief: consult an oracle shelf at your own fork; the cast lands an OODA-HA meme
help: usage: lares oracle cast [--by <kind>] [--asking <words>] [--uncertain <words>] [--observe <pointers>] [--caster <name>] [--coins <six-values>] [--fresh] [--seed <words>] (--recipe <slug> | --bag <slug>) [--realm <id>] [--face <handle>]
lares oracle cast — consult an oracle shelf at your own fork; the cast lands an OODA-HA meme
a blind throw to collide uncertainty with

The house consults an oracle whose corpus rests on a library shelf (`lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/library/oracles/<kind>/`). The kind rides as data: `by` names the shelf (the E-Jing by default), and the shelf's index record declares its own `method`, its corpus and its credits. The e-jing and doa shelves declare `three-coins`: the I Ching by three coins a line (heads three, tails two: 6 old yin and 9 old yang change, 7 and 8 hold). A new oracle joins as a shelf, never a new address or a new verb; a shelf whose method the verb runs not yet refuses by name.

Every consult lands once, as a meme under `lar:///ha.ka.ba/lares/oracle/casts/`, whose five slots run OODA-HA (`#/loop`), whatever the kind. The ask fills `#/observe` with its context pointers and `#/orient` with its gathered uncertainty and its query; the house fills `#/decide` with the throw and every reading the wiki holds, each source credited; the seat appends its reading, its move and its aftermath by slot append. The verb reads the loop's shape from the carrier the caller's stack seats for this address (a carrier a working layer seats above canon shapes the act in its place), the affordance pack its binary baked standing as the floor, and the answer names the carrier slot that shaped it. One asking, one throw: the same query by the same booked asker answers the standing cast and names the uncertainty it kept. The coins draw through the platform's entropy door, or a person types the six values thrown with real coins. The verb reads no clock: the caller names the time as testimony. A weak seed reads back: the record names a seed by a 16-hex digest anyone can test a guess against, so a person choosing one chooses a strong one.
The cast stands as a blind throw to collide uncertainty with: the throw stands, the reading stays open.

The heading `library` names where the consult reads: the oracle shelves rest among the library's holdings, the ones the `lares library` door keeps. The facet `oracle` names the shelf family it reads under, and the dynamic `speaks` names the act: the library's oracle speaks to a fork. No alias stands at an older address (early alpha burns aliases, the operator's word 2026-11-27).
